cand.title: Open Banking Expo Canada 2027
cand.excerpt: Strongest where the event has verified future dates, a Toronto venue and a clear finance/technology/leadership participant base; incumbent hotels reduce current-edition accessibility.
cand.ledgerVenue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, 255 Front Street West, Toronto

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Primary approach: Lillie Cook, Event Operations & Relationship Manager; the official team biography says she manages event operations across the portfolio. Second: Kelly Stanley, Co-founder; her biography describes planning event launches. Adam Cox, Co-founder, is an additional senior route associated with proposals and speakers. All are commercially relevant organizer contacts; none is publicly verified as the hotel contract signatory or sole accommodation buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced conference: 11 March 2027, Metro Toronto Convention Centre (MTCC), 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada; within the requested horizon. The associated pre-conference drinks are separately dated 10 March 2027, venue to be announced. No official Canada 2028 edition was located. Keep the conference date separate from the broader 10–11 March activity window.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel profile: the 157-room Harbourfront hotel is plausible for a modest delegate/speaker/VIP subset, organizer lodging or small sponsor meetings, not exclusive housing or relocation of the 700+ expected-attendee Expo. Use approximately 15–109 peak rooms only as an internal sales-sizing band, never as published demand. The supplied ~240-theatre ballroom limit excludes a 700-person plenary. This is an urban MTCC-adjacent business opportunity, not a resort programme. Official hotel marketing advertises catering and The View breakfast service, but does not establish March 2027 operational availability; the pool lounge is summer-season dependent and should not anchor a March reception proposal. Brand meeting-space counts differ from the supplied profile; obtain a current capacity sheet rather than upgrading fit.
findings.venueCommitments: Organizer-published 2027 venue is MTCC, 255 Front Street West, downtown Toronto proper, Ontario; not an outlying destination and not a competing hotel. This establishes a public venue announcement, not access to an executed contract or confirmation of contracted halls. The 2025 North Building designation must not automatically be carried into 2027.
findings.historicalRotation: Documented editions: November 2021 virtual; 17 November 2022 Toronto (physical venue unverified); 15 June 2023 MTCC Toronto; 11 June 2024 MTCC Toronto; 17 June 2025 MTCC North Building Toronto; 5 March 2026 MTCC Toronto. The 2027 edition again names MTCC Toronto. This supports repeated Toronto/MTCC use, not destination rotation or a fixed June schedule. A 2028 cycle is a prospecting inference, not an announced edition. Some secondary 2023 listings give June 14; use June 15 from Payments Canada and the organizer.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. The edition-specific Travel & Accommodation page says: “Open Banking Expo Canada will take place on March 11, 2027 at the MTCC in Toronto” and lists “MTCC, 255 Front Street West Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6 Canada.” It names no hotels, housing bureau, hotel block, booking deadline, room rate or open RFP. Every hotel listed on that page: none. This is absence of published sourcing information, not proof that hotels are uncontracted. No incumbent hotel was verified; the seed assertion that incumbent hotels limit access is not substantiated.
findings.organizationStructure: Open Banking Expo is the event brand; its official footer states it is organised by Borough Bench Media, registered in England and Wales, company number 09298718. Treat this as a corporate media/events organizer, not an association. MTCC is the venue, not the event owner or evidenced lodging buyer. No separate PCO, DMC or accommodation agency was identified in the reviewed edition materials.
findings.competitiveLimitations: MTCC is the publicly selected main-event venue; displacing the Expo into this hotel is not realistic. No sold-out hotel blocks, overflow referral programme or incumbent accommodation contracts were verified. Separate date-pressure evidence: PDAC officially runs at MTCC on 7–10 March 2027, overlapping the Expo pre-conference evening and likely arrival night. Potential availability/rate pressure is an inference, not proof of compression or overflow at Radisson.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Lillie Cook first, copying Kelly Stanley. Ask who selects/holds hotel contracts, whether 2027 rooms are already committed, all incumbent hotels/bureaux and cutoffs, out-of-town speaker/crew requirements, peak rooms/room nights, and whether March 10 drinks remain commercially contestable. After checking internal March 9–12 availability and PDAC displacement risk, offer a small flexible lodging allocation, with shoulder nights subject to confirmed need; price a modest indoor meeting/reception only after confirming attendance, catering, licensing and operational capacity. If 2027 is closed, request the next Canada-edition sourcing window and a hotel introduction/site visit. No speculative RFP or guaranteed room volume.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The 2027 event is confirmed but hotel sourcing accessibility is unconfirmed. Do not mark hotel sourcing open or committed elsewhere. Conditional routes are small organizer/speaker blocks, delegate referrals and sponsor side meetings. The 10 March drinks venue is officially “to be announced”; this does not establish an open procurement exercise. Ask whether it is already contracted before proposing an indoor venue.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated Toronto/MTCC editions justify a relationship-led bid for future lodging/referrals and small ancillary functions. There is no verified destination rotation or announced 2028 edition. Seek preferred-hotel consideration for the next Canada cycle only after obtaining the organizer’s sourcing timetable; do not represent historical venues as open inventory.
